A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Motion-2-to-3 work, and all 12 pages of each support reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix or embedded supplement; both reference supplementary material that is not included.

before.justification: v1 reports original HumanML3D evaluations, a novel-prompt user study, comparisons of data-utilization strategies, and model ablations in Tables 1–4 and Figures 4–6.

after.justification: v2 retains the original quantitative experiments and adds a Motion-X++ 3D-annotation baseline and additional qualitative comparisons.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and 4.1 retain the same local/root motion decomposition, single-view pretraining, frozen backbone with added multi-view attention and root-velocity head, triangulation, trajectory integration, and SMPL fitting.

E1.justification: Both versions use EgoExo4D/Motion-X++ videos, HumanML3D, and novel-prompt text-to-motion generation. The new 3D-annotation control reuses an existing data source, while the additional qualitative examples remain within the existing novel-prompt evaluation scenario.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds Motion-X++ 3D as a comparison baseline. Figure 4 adds evaluated MoMask and T2M-GPT outputs, including comparisons on the retained hip-hop and basketball prompts. The comparator sets in Tables 1 and 2 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds a data-source control using monocularly reconstructed 3D annotations rather than the proposed 2D-data strategy. Existing training budgets, four-view configuration, evaluation metrics, and the 15-prompt user study with 49 valid responses remain unchanged. The newly stated sequence count does not establish a training-set change.

E4.justification: Section 4.5 adds an analysis of directly using estimated 3D annotations. Figure 4 expands qualitative failure comparisons, while v1's Figure 6 and its visual model-ablation analysis are removed. The numerical pretraining, consistency-block, and view-count ablations remain unchanged in Table 4.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and user-study selection percentages without seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v2 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds Motion-X++ 3D results: R-Precision 0.596, FID 0.893, MM Dist 4.188, and Diversity 9.734. Previously tabulated values are unchanged. Figure 4 adds qualitative findings against MoMask/T2M-GPT and removes the crawl-and-stand example; Figure 6's qualitative ablation results are also removed.

T1.justification: The motion representations, tensor dimensions, camera definitions, and root-trajectory integration equation are unchanged. Neither version introduces additional formal assumptions, theoretical results, or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that disentangled 2D motion pretraining followed by multi-view learning with 3D data improves motion generation and broadens supported motion types. v2's explicit three-part contribution summary reorganizes these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 attributes the new 3D-annotation baseline's weaker results to unstable reconstructions and unrealistic estimated motion priors, contrasting these with less noisy 2D data followed by high-quality 3D learning. The existing limitations concerning noise, scale, architecture, hands, and object interactions are retained.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly specifies 102,389 training sequences, without establishing that the dataset changed. Conversely, v2 removes the abstract's public-code release statement and project link. Other implementation details remain substantially unchanged; actual code availability cannot be determined from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds a brief discussion and citation of MotionStreamer in Section 2.1. The other cited works are retained after matching renumbered references. MoMask and T2M-GPT were already cited in v1, although their evaluated comparisons are new.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites and reorganizes the abstract and introduction, adds an explicit contribution summary, and groups data-use and model-design analyses under Section 4.5. It also revises the title, author information, and acknowledgements. Most method, results discussion, limitations, and conclusion text remains intact.

P2.justification: The qualitative presentation is substantially redesigned: Figure 4 changes from a three-row comparison to an expanded multi-panel display with additional comparator columns and novel-prompt examples. Figure 6 is removed, Figure 5 moves to page 8, and Table 3 gains a baseline row and revised caption.

improvement.justification: The added 3D-annotation control in Table 3 and MoMask/T2M-GPT comparisons in Figure 4 modestly strengthen evidence for the approach, while the sequence-count disclosure improves transparency. These gains outweigh the loss of the visual ablation figure and code-access pointer, particularly because numerical model ablations remain available. Sparse implementation details for the new control and unchanged main benchmark evidence limit the improvement.
